rtd_evidence.canonical_class_normalization: present (rtd.ts resolveToolClass, added at ce51a85): ipython input.code starting with a %%bash header line resolves to canonical class 'bash'
rtd_evidence.root_cause_confirmed: The %%bash cell's actual shell command was `"C:\Users\assas\...\.venv\Scripts\python.exe" -m pytest -vv` (the absolute venv-python invocation this repo's own AGENTS.md mandates on this machine, due to a documented PYTHONHOME pollution issue). resolveToolClass correctly classified this as canonical class 'bash' with command = that same string (Phase C worked exactly as designed). But rtdEligibility's whitelist_commands check takes only the FIRST WHITESPACE-SEPARATED TOKEN of the command and compares it literally to ["pytest","git","rg","grep"]. The first token here is the quoted python.exe PATH, not the literal word "pytest" -- so eligibility resolved to reason="command" (ineligible), never reaching the size check, even though the command size (65578+ chars) was far over threshold_chars=8000. Three OTHER real commands in this session did start with a literal whitelisted first token ("git", "git", "grep") but their real outputs were all well under 8000 chars (1826 / 128 / 1289 chars), so none of them were size-eligible either. Net result: RTD never fired this pilot, and the specific reason is now known precisely -- it is a real, reproducible interaction between whitelist_commands' literal first-token matching and this project's own documented python-path invocation style, not a defect in Phase C's ipython->bash tool-class normalization (which worked exactly as designed) and not a defect in the preserve/reduce/recover pipeline itself (which was never reached to test).
